title: What the Filters Kept: 3I/ATLAS, the Loeb Overview, and a Public-Data Signal Search (EA-3I-ATLAS-NOTEBOOK-01 v1.2)
creator: Glas, Nobel; Trace, Orin
description: The working notebook of a public-data search for a signal from the interstellar object 3I/ATLAS, run 2026-11-02 to 2026-11-06 in Breakthrough Listen's public products from the Green Bank Telescope, the Allen Telescope Array, Parkes and MeerKAT, with Claude and ChatGPT as machine collaborators checking each other through code, tables and hashes. It records every search in the order the questions arose, with frozen plans, deviations, errors and nulls built as false frames. No artificial transmission is identified. One result stands unresolved: thirteen comet-frame coincidence clusters at 1665.53–1668.46 MHz in the Green Bank cadence of 2025-12-18, reproducible under an independent implementation, sensitive to normalization and threshold, unreplicated in sixteen held-out channels and at Parkes. The findings that hold concern representation: a Google AI Overview that presented Avi Loeb's held Level 4 position as a concession; the ATA paper's positive drift window against the negative drift its stated acceleration gives a tone on the object; a public statement that dropped the search's frequency and drift scope; a header read as a measurement. The archive's instruments are set against the record (instrument-conditioned nullity, correlated blind spots, model independence, disciplinary model collapse, frame conversion), and the sophistry measure is run for the first time. All code and results are filed for rerun.
content_type: Notebook; working record of a public-data technosignature search (Transactions on Substrate Engineering); frozen plans, results and files
substrate: AI-assisted (substrate). Written under the heteronyms Nobel Glas and Orin Trace. The investigation was run by Lee Sharks with two machine collaborators on the same public data: Claude (Anthropic), which ran the Green Bank, Parkes and MeerKAT searches and the frozen runs and composed the notebook in session on 2026-11-02 to 2026-11-06; and ChatGPT (OpenAI), whose ATA searches, audits of the thirteen and C03 reports Lee supplied and are filed as written (chatgpt/). Each system's results were checked by the other through code and tables. The questions, the rulings on the Overview and on Loeb, the authorship and venue, and the decision to deposit are Lee Sharks's, quoted verbatim in §12. The revisions on three outside reviews (DeepSeek once, ChatGPT twice) are recorded in §13.
methodology: Breakthrough Listen's public 3I/ATLAS products only, fetched by name; a directory that refused access was out of scope. Every test that decides anything had its plan written, hashed and committed before the counts it decides, its departures recorded before any count they could affect; plans frozen on data already examined are marked as such, and looks without a frozen plan are marked exploratory and change no verdict. Every null is a set of false frames built the same way as the true one (false range-accelerations, beam swaps, role permutations, time shuffles, phase randomization, rigid frequency shifts), each family read on its own. A frozen procedure, data not read before, and independent reproduction are stated apart for every result. Quotations are checked at their offsets against saved sources.
falsification_conditions: A frozen plan's hash not matching its committed file, or a count shown to precede its plan; a script rerun on its named public inputs not reproducing a stated count; the thirteen shown to arise from a processing step the record omits; GBT telemetry placing scan 0017 off target beyond the beam; the ATA's executed filter shown to keep the negative drift class; a quoted passage not saying what the notebook quotes.

wiki_article: What the Filters Kept (EA-3I-ATLAS-NOTEBOOK-01, version 1.2) is the working notebook of a public-data search for a signal from the interstellar object 3I/ATLAS, written under the heteronyms Nobel Glas and Orin Trace and deposited in the Crimson Hexagonal Archive on 6 November 2026 for Transactions on Substrate Engineering. The investigation ran from 2 to 6 November 2026 on Breakthrough Listen's public products from the Green Bank Telescope, the Allen Telescope Array, Parkes and MeerKAT, with Lee Sharks directing two machine collaborators, Claude and ChatGPT, who checked each other's work through code, candidate tables and hashes. Every deciding test had its plan frozen and hashed before its counts, and every null was built as a set of false frames constructed the same way as the true one. The notebook identifies no artificial transmission. It reports one unresolved result: thirteen comet-frame coincidence clusters near 1666 MHz in the Green Bank cadence of 18 December 2025, which reproduce under an independent implementation, depend on normalization and threshold, and do not replicate in sixteen held-out channels or at Parkes. Its findings that hold concern representation: a Google AI Overview presented Avi Loeb's position, held at Level 4 of his scale from July 2025, as a later concession; the Allen Telescope Array paper filters for positive drift where its stated acceleration gives a tone on the object a negative one; and a public statement of that search's null dropped its frequency and drift scope. The notebook sets the archive's instruments against the record, among them instrument-conditioned nullity, correlated blind spots, disciplinary model collapse and frame conversion, and runs the sophistry measure for the first time. Its companion is Lee Sharks's public account A Firm No (#1743). Version 1.1, the same day, records the operator's reading that the published searches were built to rule a signal out at the least cost without the work ruling out requires. Version 1.2 (6 November 2026) makes factual repairs in place: MeerKAT's technosignature search, with its limit of 0.17 W over 900 to 1670 MHz (ATel #17499), is added as a fourth published search, and the notebook's citations of Loeb's April essay and of the PER-D rubric are corrected.

defines_concepts.definition: In EA-3I-ATLAS-NOTEBOOK-01, a search that sums spectral power along the path a tone fixed on a moving object takes across the scans of a cadence, below any per-scan detection threshold, and counts clusters kept in every on-source scan, against nulls built as false frames the same way.

In EA-3I-ATLAS-NOTEBOOK-01, the null of a frame-dependent search: the same procedure run under false range-accelerations, swapped beams, permuted scan roles, shuffled rows, randomized phases or shifted frequencies, each family read on its own and none pooled as one calibrated background.
